analysis:
This batch contains only markdown changes: four new changelog.d entries and a docs addition to docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (lines 248-253, the systemAvailable formula). No executable source is supplied, so the described behavior changes cannot be verified here.

Changelog claims that matter for the next pass, none of which is a finding on the supplied evidence:
- GLM-5.3-Flash accepts strict tools, JSON mode and forced tool choice with no constrained decoding. The docs say output is withheld until it is schema-validated, with a 422 on failure. The implementation must fail closed and must not stream unvalidated content. This relates to T-008 and TB-002.
- Logprobs are enabled on GLM. Typed 400 refusals for MiMo logprobs and token constraints are said to be applied before any reservation. The implementation should confirm these 400s come before reservation and do not leak data.
- Variable-frame-rate video indexing needs bounded frame counts and decode memory. This touches T-050 and media handling in TB-003.
- Page cache and purgeable pages now count as available memory in load admission. The docs state the new figure is max(old free+inactive, free-speculative+external+purgeable) and is never stricter than before. This loosens the admission gate. If macOS does not actually drop the page cache promptly, a load could over-commit. That is an availability and robustness matter in TB-007, T-029 and the hardware-support invariants. The docs say the final atomic pending-load permit and the post-load KVHeadroomProbe still apply. The code paths (SystemMemory.availableBytes, ModelLoadAdmission) were not supplied. Recommend verifying that speculative_count cannot underflow and that the free-only override works.

No changes to encryption, attestation, authorization, or the prefix-cache (T-041) were visible in the supplied files. The coordinator-side acceptance of the new capabilities (forced tool choice for glm-5.3-flash) is platform-owned and outside this scope.
